purpose: Runs Squire's check-in command as the session would when the owner asks, checks wakeUps in the owner's squire.json after a set, a change, a stop and a rhythm (typical and heavy), checks the wake-up router's scheduler run reads a check-in set this way, and checks a time or rhythm the router could not read is never written.
title: Check-ins set, changed and stopped by asking

testCases.description: A check-in asked for is set in wakeUps as the router reads it, and the scheduler's run reads it
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/check-ins-by-asking.test.js::a check-in the owner asks for is set in their squire.json in the form the check-ins are read from, nothing else in it changes, and the scheduler's run reads it

testCases.description: A check-in asked to move is changed, one asked to stop is removed, the rest unchanged
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/check-ins-by-asking.test.js::a check-in the owner asks to move is changed, and one they ask to stop is removed, and the rest stay as they were

testCases.description: A rhythm more often than hourly is set as asked, with one sentence that it uses the plan faster
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/check-ins-by-asking.test.js::a rhythm more often than hourly is set as asked, with one plain sentence that frequent check-ins use the plan faster; hourly or slower carries no such sentence

testCases.description: A check-in the router could not read is never written; Squire says why
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/check-ins-by-asking.test.js::a time the check-ins cannot be read at, no words, a rhythm of no minutes, or a change or stop of a check-in that is not there is never written: Squire says why and the settings are unchanged

testCases.description: A check-in from the session is asked naming its time and words; any other spelling is refused; a squire.json Edit is asked
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/check-ins-by-asking.test.js::the session sets a check-in only on the owner's yes: the check-in command is asked first, naming the time and the words; spelt any other way it is refused, yes or no; and an Edit of the owner's squire.json is asked

testCases.description: a look-alike spelling of the check-in command the Mac opens as the same file is asked as the check-in it is, naming the time and words, in both modes
testCases.testPointer: tests/acceptance/check-ins-by-asking.test.js::a look-alike spelling of the check-in command that the Mac opens as the same file (a long s for its last s) is the check-in command: it is asked as a check-in, naming the time and the words, never as an unknown command, in the default mode and in auto mode
